subject: Renewal proposal: sprint-topup + commit smoothing for NovaWeb
messages:
From: Lisa Bowman <lisa@novaweb.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning — Q4 surge and top-up ask

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the heads-up that our renewal window is coming up. We've run several spike campaigns in the last 6 weeks and are projecting a 20-30% temporary uplift in token consumption during peak quarters (Q4). Before we lock in next year's commit we'd like to explore a short-term top-up + smoothing approach so we don't get hit with large overages while still moving toward a multi-quarter commit.

High-level asks: 
- Can Redwood hold current unit pricing for Q4 while we validate the uplift (price hold through 12/31/2026)?
- Provide a sprint-topup (one-off credit) to cover anticipated Q4 surge — targeting an incremental 15% capacity (non-recurring credits).
- Options for proration and billing (we want clear visibility on how a partial commit or mid-quarter uplift would be invoiced).

I copied our procurement lead (procurement@novaweb.com) and Jake (engineering) — they will handle PO and SOW questions.

If you can send a short options matrix (recommended, risk, billing impact) and a notional DocuSign-ready SOW we can review this week, that would be ideal.

Best,
Lisa
Lisa Bowman
Head of Product — NovaWeb Inc.

---

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Bowman <lisa@novaweb.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal planning — Q4 surge and top-up ask

Lisa — thanks for the clarity. Appreciate the heads-up on the Q4 surge. Attached is a concise options matrix and a proposal (RI_Renewal_SprintTopup_v3.pdf). TL;DR of the three paths we recommend: 

Option A — Commit uplift (6-month bridge):
- 30% temporary uplift to baseline commit for 6 months, billed as committed usage.
- Price hold guaranteed for Q4 and Q1 following the uplift.
- Benefit: lowest unit cost and avoids overage unpredictability.

Option B — Sprint-topup credits (one-off, non-recurring):
- 15% capacity in prepurchased credits applied to token overages during Q4.
- No long-term commit required; credits expire 1/31/2027.
- Benefit: fastest to agree and immediate overage protection.

Option C — Hybrid (staged commit + credits):
- Small, multi-quarter commit increase (15%) + 10% sprint credits for Q4.
- Price hold for Q4.
- Benefit: balances flexibility and unit-cost improvement.

Notes on billing/proration: 
- Any commit uplift that starts mid-billing period will be prorated daily for the initial invoice.
- Credits are deducted before applying overage rates.
- We can structure invoicing monthly or net-30 consolidated.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Tell us preferred option (A/B/C) by EOD Wed 8/4.
2) If Option A or C, Marissa (cc'd) will draft amendment language for legal to review.
3) If Option B, we can issue a credit invoice and updated SOW for signature immediately.

Attachments: RI_Renewal_SprintTopup_v3.pdf (options matrix), NovaWeb_SOW_Q4.xlsx (SOW template).

Jonas Weber
Lead, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

---

From: Jake Morris <jake@novaweb.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Lisa Bowman <lisa@novaweb.com>, procurement@novaweb.com
Date: 2026-07-30T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — Q4 surge and top-up ask

Jonas — quick Q on Option B and the credit flow. On behalf of procurement: 
- If we buy credits, how will they appear on the invoice? (line-item? prepayment?)
- We need to remove any automatic true-up within the SOW — procurement cannot sign off on auto-increase clauses without explicit approvals.
- Also need clarity on proration if credits are applied mid-billing cycle.

Uploading our PO template (attached). If you can show an example invoice line and confirm no auto-trueup language, we can route a PO quickly.

Thanks,
Jake
Procurement Manager — NovaWeb

(On Thu, Jul 29, 2026 at 11:03 AM Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com> wrote:)
> Lisa — thanks for the clarity. Appreciate the heads-up on the Q4 surge. Attached is a concise options matrix and a proposal (RI_Renewal_SprintTopup_v3.pdf). TL;DR of the three paths we recommend: ...

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jake Morris <jake@novaweb.com>, Lisa Bowman <lisa@novaweb.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — Q4 surge and top-up ask

Jake / Lisa — thanks for the PO template. Quick answers to procurement bullets below and proposed legal guardrails so procurement can sign.

Invoice & credits: 
- Credits are issued as a prepayment line item on the invoice ("Sprint Top-up Credit") and applied against overage before calculating any overage rate. Example invoice line provided in pricing-comparison.csv attached.
- If credits are purchased up-front they will appear as a single line item (prepayment) and be reconciled monthly until exhausted.

On automatic true-up / SOW language: 
- We will remove any automatic consumption-triggered contract increases. Any change to the committed quantity will require written acceptance (email or DocuSign) from NovaWeb procurement.
- We will include a mutually agreeable notification window (14 days) before any suggested commit adjustments and separate approval flow in the amendment.

Proration: 
- Mid-period commit uplifts are prorated daily for the invoice period; credits apply effective the day they are posted.

Legal / timeline: 
- I will ask our legal ops to produce an amendment with explicit approval gates (no auto-trueup). Jonas will share the DocuSign link once we have the final SOW.
- Proposed timeline if you want to lock the Q4 price hold: sign amendment + purchase credits (if Option B) by Aug 9 to ensure processing and credit posting before 9/1.

If you prefer, Option B can be the fastest path — Redwood can issue a credit invoice the same week we get a signed PO. Option A will take a few extra days for amendment and legal review but gives the best unit economics.

Action items: 
- Jake / procurement: confirm whether you want Option A, B, or C by COB 8/4.
- NovaWeb: return signed PO or indicate required SOW redlines by 8/6.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call this week to finalize.

Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Operations — Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0222

Attachments referenced: RI_Renewal_SprintTopup_v3.pdf (proposal), NovaWeb_SOW_Q4.xlsx (SOW template), pricing-comparison.csv (invoice example), NovaWeb_PO_Template.pdf (from procurement).
